Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0802 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Valid 270100Z - 271200Z

...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS PORTIONS OF THE
UPPER MIDWEST AND WESTERN GREAT LAKES...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of large to very large hail, damaging
winds (possibly 75+ mph), and tornado risk remain likely from the
upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes southwestward into
Nebraska, mainly late this evening and tonight.

...Upper Midwest...
A very unstable environment remains in place across the region, with
the MPX, GRB, and DVN 00Z soundings sampling MLCAPE from 3100, 2900,
and 2800 J/kg, respectively. Surface observations show mid to upper
70s dewpoints on the warm side of the warm front extending from
north-central MN through northeast WI/far western Upper MI. A
thunderstorm has matured upstream of this corridor, with the
expectation it will remain strong to severe as it continues
southeastward. Modest low-level warm advection into this boundary
will also contribute to additional thunderstorms this evening and
overnight. Environmental conditions are still expected to support
large to very large hail early in the convective cycle while a more
cellular mode is likely. Thereafter, a trend towards bowing segments
capable of severe wind gusts is anticipated. A singular MCS could
eventually develop, with severe gusts possible as it moves southward
as well. Some gusts, both within the line segments and early in the
MCS lifecycle, could be significant (i.e. over 75 mph).

...TN Valley...
A cold-pool-driven MCS continues to propagate south-southeast at
approximately 40 kts. The downstream airmass is very moist, with
numerous sites reporting dewpoints in the low 80s. This moisture is
contributing to extreme buoyancy, with the recent 00Z BNA sounding
sampling 4500 J/kg of SBCAPE. This MCS is also oriented
perpendicular to the deep-layer vertical shear. All of these factors
will contribute to continued southward progression, with an
attendant risk for strong gusts likely extending into Middle TN this
evening.

...South-Central into Southeast SD into central NE...
Numerous attempts at deep convection along the weak surface trough
extending from south-central SD through central NE have failed thus
far. The window of opportunity for deep convection will likely
remain open for the next hour or two before building inhibition
associated with nocturnal cooling precludes mature convection. Until
that occurs, there remains a conditional risk for severe
thunderstorms capable of strong downdrafts and isolated large hail.

...Elsewhere...
Increasing thunderstorm coverage is possible across the Mid-Atlantic
over the next few hours as a shortwave trough progresses
southeastward across the region. Moderate vertical shear could
support updraft organization with deeper, more persistent
convection. Isolated damaging gusts and hail are possible with the
more organized storms. Isolated damaging gusts remain possible
across northern Wyoming and far southwest South Dakota as high-based
thunderstorms track northeastward across the region this evening.
Jackson Hole Wyoming reported a gust of 50 kt at 2353Z.

..Mosier.. 07/27/2026

Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1213 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE GREAT
LAKES INTO PARTS OF THE OHIO VALLEY...

...SUMMARY...
Severe storms capable of damaging winds and large hail are possible
across the Great Lakes into the Ohio Valley Monday into Monday
night. More sporadic occurrences of damaging wind appear possible in
the Mid-Atlantic, Tennessee Valley, central High Plains, and
southeast Arizona.

...Great Lakes southward across the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys...
Early day storms are possible from southern WI into northern IL
Monday, associated with a warm advection regime at 850 mb with
modest westerly winds at that level. The overall severe risk is
expected to be marginal for hail or wind with any such activity.

Later in the day, a surface trough is forecast to develop roughly
from Lake Huron southwestward into southern WI/northern IL, and
southwesterly low-level winds will continue to spread moisture
eastward into Lower MI, IN and OH. Scattered cells are forecast to
develop near this surface trough/wind shift, aided by the late upper
trough amplification. Storms are expected from eastern WI across
Lake MI and into Lower MI by late afternoon, and supercell mode
appears most likely given up to 50 kt deep-layer shear. A low-level
jet out of the west at over 30 kt is expected over IL, with
increasing speeds into IN and OH into the evening as the upper
trough amplifies and convection possibly merges into clusters or an
MCS. Models vary on how much storm coverage will extend into IL,
with the most likely areas from southeast WI across southern Lake MI
and into southern Lower MI, northern IN and OH.

Despite relatively warm conditions aloft, the elongated hodographs
from mid to upper levels, and substantial boundary-layer moisture
suggest cells may produce large hail. A tornado or two may occur as
well late afternoon through early evening, with storm mergers
overnight aiding outflow/severe gust potential. A categorical
upgrade is possible for parts of the risk area in later outlooks as
predictability increases.

...Central High Plains...
Weak high pressure will exist over the northern Plains with a front
pushing south across I-80. Surface winds will back to eastern late
in the day, with corridor of higher dewpoints over southern NE and
northern KS, extending into northeast CO.

Strong heating will occur beneath the upper ridge, and an uncapped
and unstable air mass will develop. Apart from the monsoonal regime
over the Rockies, additional multicellular storms are expected after
21Z from northeast CO into southwest NE and northwest KS. The hot
temperatures near the moist plume and weak flow aloft will support
locally severe outflow winds.

...Southeast Arizona...
Isolated severe gusts cannot be ruled out over far southeast AZ as
midlevel moisture and daytime heating leads to scattered storms over
the higher terrain. Cells are expected to move northwestward, with
PWAT over 1.25" and steep low-level lapse rates supporting strong
outflows.

..Jewell.. 07/26/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0219 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE SOUTHERN
MID ATLANTIC INTO NORTH CAROLINA AND THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of damaging winds and isolated hail are
possible from the southern Mid-Atlantic into the Carolinas and
central and southern Appalachians Tuesday into Tuesday evening.
Isolated severe wind gusts may occur in the central High Plains.

...Southern Mid Atlantic into North Carolina and southern
Appalachians...
An upper trough with a 40-50 kt midlevel speed max will push
southeastward across the Appalachians and into parts of the Mid
Atlantic and Carolinas during the day, supporting thunderstorms
through much of the period.

Storms are expected to be ongoing early Tuesday from PA and WV into
eastern KY, near a cold front. This activity should persist as it
moves into MD/VA/NC, where a surface trough will deepen. Daytime
heating along with ample low-level moisture will support 1500-2000
J/kg MLCAPE, and winds will be veering with height, supporting a few
supercells. Despite warm temperatures aloft, the 40-50 kt deep-layer
shear may support hail in the strongest cells. In addition,
southwesterly 850 mb winds up to 40 kt late in the day may yield an
isolated tornado risk from southeast VA into NC. Moderately high
PWAT along with steep low-level lapse rates during the peak heating
hours will also support locally damaging wind gusts.

...Northern High Plains...
Instability will increase over eastern WY, western SD/NE and
northeast CO during the afternoon as a weak surface trough develops.
Southeast surface winds will maintain 50s to lower 60s F dewpoints,
with storms forming after 21Z near the higher terrain in WY/CO.
South to southeast storm motions may bring multicellular storms
across western NE and northeast CO during the evening with a few
severe gusts possible.

..Jewell.. 07/26/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0332 AM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Valid 291200Z - 031200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Wednesday...

The large-scale pattern will feature an upper high over the southern
High Plains with ridging extending into the northern Plains and
upper MS Valley. Meanwhile, broader-scale troughing will persist
across the eastern CONUS, anchored by an upper low over the
Mid-Atlantic. 

A very moist air mass is expected to contribute to moderate to
strong instability by afternoon along a cold front over the
Southeast. While vertical shear will remain rather weak, the strong
buoyancy will be supportive of locally intense downdrafts capable of
damaging winds. Elsewhere, a few strong to severe storms appear
possible within a moist upslope regime over the central High Plains,
as well as along a cold front moving into the northern High Plains.


...Days 5 and 6/Thursday and Friday...

The southwestern U.S. ridge/eastern U.S. trough configuration will
be maintained this period. Between those features, a notable
short-wave trough is forecast to track from the northern Plains into
the mid MS Valley along with a surface frontal system.  Persistent
low-level ridging from the Great Lakes into the Gulf Coast states
will limit the breadth of an unstable warm sector to the northern
and central Plains on Thursday, where thunderstorms are expected.
Vertical shear is not forecast to be particularly strong; however,
some potential exists for an organized severe weather episode.
Additional strong to severe storms appear possible along the front
in the Ozarks on Friday. Both days will continue to be monitored for
the possible inclusion of severe weather probabilities in subsequent
forecasts.


...Days 7 and 8/Saturday and Sunday...

There is good agreement across the ensemble means in the progression
of a more significant short-wave trough from western into central
Canada with the southern fringe of more substantial height falls
overspreading the northern Rockies into the northern High Plains on
Sunday. That upper-air system will be attended by a cold front that
could be the source of severe storm development in those areas
Sunday afternoon into night.

..Mead.. 07/26/2026
